story.title: The Army Reaches the Sea
story.text: The waves were too rough — the emperor stood on shore, afraid to board.
story.narration: The Tang army of three hundred thousand reached the sea. Wave after wave came rolling in, and the emperor stood on the shore worrying: if the ship tossed like that, who could bear the crossing?

story.title: A New “Great Camp” by the Sea
story.text: The emperor walked in smiling, and the ground under him never moved.
story.narration: General Xue Rengui had a great camp built of bright cloth, with a banquet laid out inside. The emperor walked in smiling and sat down perfectly steady. Then the curtain lifted — the camp had been floating on the sea all along, and the emperor had already crossed.

keyMoment.question: To get the emperor across without his noticing, what should the ship be dressed up as?

options.hint: A warship tells everyone that something big is coming.
A raft bobs about — the emperor would see through it at once.

keyMoment.reveal: The plainer the look, the less anyone suspects it.

misconceptions: Crossing the sea under camouflage is not cheating: it puts a big thing inside an ordinary look
Not everything is solved by being strong

quiz.question: What did Xue Rengui disguise the ship as?
quiz.explanation: A camp was the plainest thing of all — the emperor walked in and never suspected a thing.

quiz.question: For a big thing that everyone would notice, which way is most like crossing the sea under camouflage?
options: Tuck it quietly into something you do every day
Leave it until the very last day
quiz.explanation: The plainer the look, the less anyone suspects it — the big thing hides inside the ordinary.
